files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller checklist

Owner: P. Guerrero. Complete in sequence; no skipping ahead.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, prepare one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 that pays in July. If one exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities; note that some months every payroll run pays in-month.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule, supporting contracts, and the GL. If it has not been recorded, book ONE combined journal entry and do not duplicate an existing entry. Apply the convention that a full month is taken in the month each prepaid item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after verifying the GL to prevent duplication.
5. Check the June vendor-bill documents against the GL expense coding. Reclass anything miscoded to the correct expense account.
6. After items 1-5 are posted, prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Bluewater Stack Co. began in 2019 when two former operations leads grew tired of watching small service teams coordinate customer work through sprawling spreadsheets, inbox threads, and improvised status meetings. They built a lightweight internal tool, shared it with a few peers, and discovered that the same problem appeared across agencies, consultancies, and distributed project teams.

Today, Bluewater Stack Co. sells a cloud-based workflow platform that brings client intake, recurring task management, approvals, and operational reporting into one place. The product is deliberately practical: quick to configure, easy for nontechnical users to understand, and flexible enough to fit the way a team already works. Customers also receive implementation guidance and ongoing support from people who know the product firsthand.

The company remains a small SaaS business with a close-knit, slightly informal team. Product and support compare notes constantly, salespeople are expected to understand real customer workflows, and internal chat tends to mix careful release planning with strong opinions about coffee and keyboard shortcuts.

Bluewater Stack Co. is currently balancing steady customer service with routine product improvements and a refreshed marketing effort. The team is tightening operating processes, documenting institutional knowledge, and preparing for the next phase of measured growth while continuing business as usual.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## Direction

Make Bluewater Stack Co. easier to recognize and easier to understand. The story should stay grounded in practical workflow problems rather than broad transformation language.

## Priorities

- Refresh the core brand presentation across the website, sales materials, and customer-facing templates.
- Publish customer-led content showing how small teams replace spreadsheet-heavy operating routines.
- Run two educational webinars per quarter, with topics shared across product, support, and sales.
- Pilot a partner co-marketing program with complementary consultants and service providers.
- Build a reusable library of short product demonstrations for campaigns and sales follow-up.

## Audience and message

Focus on operations leaders, client-service managers, and founders who need clearer ownership and fewer manual handoffs. Lead with fast adoption, flexible workflows, and responsive support.

## Working cadence

Campaign themes will be planned by quarter. Marketing will meet regularly with sales and support to review common objections, customer language, and promising stories. Webinar follow-up should be timely and useful rather than overly promotional.

## Measures

Track qualified conversations, webinar engagement, partner-sourced interest, content reuse by sales, and conversion through the evaluation journey. Final channel emphasis remains subject to the Q2 close and team capacity.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# A few handoff notes from your predecessor

P. Guerrero — a few things worth knowing before you settle into the June close:

- The bank's own service fees and charges usually show up near the end of the statement. We have historically picked those up as part of the close, so give the final statement pages a careful look.
- June vendor-bill coding deserves a second pass. Some expenses may have been posted to the wrong accounts; when the GL and the paperwork disagree, the documents in `bills/` are authoritative.
- The budget was fixed early in the quarter. The one-off June items were never planned, and they are generally the reason the larger budget-to-actual variances look so pronounced.
- Payroll timing matters this month: the back half of June pays in early July. The payroll register contains the relevant dates, so use it when determining the accrual.
